links.comparator_used: Offer as built (free-form message on a fixed schedule, regardless of window state), plus waiting for the window to reopen and a reply prompt, evaluated by model-based offline evaluation
links.outcome: Delivery of the offer to speak with a medical professional to mothers whose 24-hour window had closed
links.effect: Sending the offer as an approved template was estimated to reach 81.5 to 86.8 in 100 such mothers, versus 0.3 in 100 as built, 16.6 for waiting and 11.6 for a reply prompt. Free-form failure jumped by 93.0 percentage points (95% CI 87.0 to 99.1) at 24 hours.
links.tradeoff: Outcomes are deliveries, not health outcomes. Evaluation was model-based and offline, with bounds for unconfirmed delivery. Opting out did not rise with message volume. Tabular Q-learning converged to the same template rule and did not beat it in any of 13 stress tests, so the gain needed no learning.
links.quote: Model-based offline evaluation, with bounds for unconfirmed delivery, estimates that sending the offer as an approved template would reach 81.5 to 86.8 in 100 such mothers, against 16.6 for waiting and 11.6 for a reply prompt.

design_hint: window-aware message scheduling using approved templates
